label: paragraph_title
text: SATURDAY CAUSERIE

label: text
text: Whilst anti-British feeling in Kwangtung has not, as H.E. the Governor remarked yesterday, completely disappeared, there are indications that the merchants there are becoming more confident that the calling off of the strike pickets indicates the complete removal of all hindrances to free and unfettered intercourse in all goods between the two ports. If the “indications” consisted merely of reported opinions without anything practical to bear them out, there would be logic in the arguments of the pessimists who still refuse to believe that the boycott of British goods is a thing of the past. But already ships are beginning to, berth at the Canton wharves and have been able to get labour for loading without interference.

label: text
text: A certain amount of cargo has moved since the declaration and the day may not be far distant when the godowns in Hong Kong will cease to harbour goods which, having been sold but not taken up, have been a heavy charge on the local import and export firms. The tone of optimism in the speeches which introduced the Budget for the coming year is merely the reflection of opinion in responsible circles in both ports. Merchants are confident that complete restoration of normal trade channels is only a question of time. The people of Kwangtung need the materials which ships from this port can supply them and markets which are open from here. Eventually, boycott or no boycott, the need would have

label: text
text: asserted itself in time. The declaration calling off picket interference has merely expedited matters and now it is for merchants and shipping firms to endeavour to the best of their ability to make good the opportunities which have been withheld them during a period which has been as trying to the majority in Canton as it has to those whose interests have suffered in Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Essentially an "economy" budget (for it was drafted at a time when conditions with regard to the Boycott were far from favourable). It is surprising that the only branch of work which should have been chosen for the "axe" was that of "Public Works" Recurrent." Faced with a heavy deficit on the 1926 year's working which will depreciate considerably the Colony's reserves, it was only natural to expect that the policy of retrenchment would be uniform throughout the various departments. So far from allowing for savings elsewhere, however, the amount saved on abandoning temporarily such vitally important works as the laying of pipes across the harbour to ensure an adequate water supply and the construction of a jail to supercede one which is a standing disgrace by reason of its inadequate accommodation, was even eaten into by expenditure in other directions. That the retrenchment which affected very considerably the Education Department last year was only regarded as necessary during the continuation of abnormal conditions is generally recognised. But whether the pendulum has swung sufficiently far back as to justify the increased expenditure on local education which the Budget contemplates is a matter for considerable doubt in view of the "sober" optimism which in other directions finds expression in a policy of caution.

label: paragraph_title
text: WUCHANG TREACHERY.

label: paragraph_title
text: Northern General Seeks Safety of U.S. Flag.

label: text
text: Through treachery the southern forces at length have captured Wuchang after breakdown of plans for evacuation which brought about a brief artillery battle, final engagement of the siege.

label: text
text: At 4 a.m. to day, northern troops inside Wuchang's walls who secretly had been negotiating with the southerners suddenly opened three gates of the city admitting about 3,000 southern soldiers who after a brisk exchange of rifle fire advanced carrying everything before them.

label: text
text: In taking over the city, they placed in custody General Lu Yu, chun, the northern commander, and his staff, although on the appearance of the foe General Lu sought safety under the American flag fleeing into the home of Dr. A. M. Sherman, Principal of Central China University.

label: text
text:
Evacuation of the city by the northern forces was to have taken place on October 9 as the besieged northerners had accepted terms laid down by their foes and were to have been incorporated, into the army of General Liu Tso-lung at Chingshan, seven miles down the river from the city.
Although the terms that the southerners laid down defined what disposition was to be made of small arms no mention was made of artillery. Therefore when the northerners began to leave the city they undertook to take with them their artillery and began loading it on lighters to be transported down the river.
Seeing this the artillery at Han-yang arsenal went into action and cannon from Wuchang answered frustrating the plans laid down for the evacuation. It was while negotiators were busy making new arrangements for the southerners to take possession of the city that the actual occupation took place at 4 a.m. when the soldiers inside threw open the gates.

label: paragraph_title
text: MACAO'S GOOD NEWS.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” learns from Macao that the Chinese-owned steamer “Shing Cheong,” (Capt. Francisco Marques), flying the Portuguese flag, completed her round trip to Canton and back without any incident.

label: text
text: The “Shing Cheong” took 200 Chinese passengers from Macao to Canton and was the first river steamer to berth at her wharf since the boycott.

label: text
text: On the same day (Wednesday) as the "Shing Cheong's" departure for Canton, a Chinese passenger tow-boat left Shekki also for"Canton. The tow carried on her initial trip over 200 passengers and a cargo of 1,400 picals of saltfish.

label: text
text: The passenger-boat service between Macao and Kongmoon was resumed on Thursday. The Chinese merchants and traders are in high spirits over the resumption of the services with Canton.

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON REQUEST FOR REPLACEMENT:

label: text
text: EQUALITY AGITATION

label: text
text:
Certain Chinese treaties with Great Britain, Japan, the U.S.A., Italy, Spain and Portugal expire this year (says a correspondent in the "Canton Gazette") also treaties with Annam (the foreign relations of which are directed by France,) and with Belgium.
The agitation for their replacement by agreements in which the sovereign rights of China shall be recognised is therefore most timely. It is significant that with the exception of groups bound by financial or political dependence on the foreign imperialists all classes of Chinese are united in urging the termination of such Unequal Treaties, continues the writer.

label: text
text: Other extracts from this article are:—

label: text
text: The nations involved are all, with the exception of Annam, signatories of the Washington Conference. France, which controls Annam, was also a signatory so that the good faith and the given word of all these countries are at stake in their attitude on this matter. Each of these nations at that gathering solemnly bound itself to recognise the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of the Chinese Republic.

label: paragraph_title
text: The Acid Test.

label: text
text: The demand for the revision of these treaties on a basis of equality to include the giving up of the special privileges enjoyed by the nationals of these countries will test the sincerity of the nations concerned. If these refuse to enact new treaties on such a basis they will prove that all their protestations of friendship for the Chinese are only talk, or "bunk" as the Americans would term it. This is certainly a case where "actions speak louder than words."

label: text
text: Anxiety was allayed shortly before midnight as to the safety of the s.s. "Borneo" which, with a cargo of coal consigned to the Taikoo Sugar Refinery, was reported yesterday as overdue.

label: text
text: The vessel arrived off Taikoo at 11.45 p.m.' yesterday.

label: text
text: It appears, from the report of the master, that the ship, which sailed from Honggy at daylight on October 10, experienced a strong N.N.E. gale in Tongking Gulf and have to for eleven hours. Shelter was also taken in Kami Bay and Ponchin Bay for over four hours.

label: text
text: In the China Sea, nearing St. John's Island, a strong monsoon with heavy seas was experienced, this also contributing to the delay.

label: text
text: Having no wireless, the ship was unable to communicate its position.
